concepts.def: The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity: 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System, containing 99.86% of its mass.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.
Sun-centred model of the Solar System established by Copernicus in 1543.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Early Models of the Solar System — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Early Models of the Solar System brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Early Models of the Solar System.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
